original_question: For a fixed integer k ≥ 2, let ex(n, C2k) denote the Turán number of the even cycle C2k, meaning the maximum number of edges in an n-vertex graph containing no copy of C2k. Does there exist a positive constant c such that ex(n, C2k) ≥ c n^(1+1/k)?
target_in_paper: Section 2, under the heading "Erdős conjecture 2" (unnumbered conjecture, p. 4): Erdős conjectured that there exists a positive constant c such that ex(n, C_{2k}) >= c n^(1+1/k).
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's intended target almost exactly: it uses the same extremal function ex(n, C_{2k}), the same forbidden subgraph C_{2k}, and the same lower-bound order n^(1+1/k) as the conjecture stated at the start of Section 2. The added phrase "for a fixed integer k >= 2" is consistent with the surrounding context and makes the dependence on k clearer than the paper's brief formulation.
missing_details: The paper's ambient graph class is finite simple graphs: ex(n, H) is defined as the maximum number of edges in an n-vertex graph containing no copy of H as a subgraph.
The constant should be made explicit as depending on k, i.e. c = c(k) > 0; this dependence is implicit in the paper and is consistent with the nearby upper bound ex(n, C_{2k}) <= c_k n^(1+1/k).

The quantifier over n is left implicit in your draft; to make the question fully stand-alone, one should specify whether the inequality is intended for all sufficiently large n (the natural asymptotic reading in this context).
It helps to state explicitly that C_{2k} denotes the cycle of length 2k.
refined_question: For each fixed integer k >= 2, let ex(n, C_{2k}) be the Turán number of the cycle C_{2k}, that is, the maximum number of edges in a finite simple n-vertex graph containing no subgraph isomorphic to C_{2k}. Is it true that there exists a constant c = c(k) > 0 such that ex(n, C_{2k}) >= c n^(1+1/k) for all sufficiently large n?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, using the notation of Section 1, if m_i(n) denotes the number of i-cycles in the complete graph K_n, then ex(n, C_{2k}) = f(0, 0, m_3(n), ..., m_{2k-1}(n), 0, m_{2k+1}(n), ..., m_n(n)); the question is whether this special case of f(a_1, ..., a_n) is bounded below by c(k) n^(1+1/k).
justification: The draft clearly targets the even-cycle Turán problem, not the repeated-cycle-length problems in Section 1 or Hajós' conjecture in Section 3. The exact matching statement appears at the beginning of Section 2 under "Erdős conjecture 2". Section 1 supplies the formal definition of ex(n, H) and explicitly rewrites ex(n, C_k) as a special case of the cycle-distribution extremal function f(a_1, ..., a_n). The nearby Theorem 2.1 gives the matching upper-bound exponent 1 + 1/k, confirming that the conjecture is about the correct asymptotic order and that the constant is understood to depend on k. So the sharp paper-faithful refinement is the same conjecture, with the graph class, dependence c = c(k), and asymptotic quantifier over n stated explicitly.

citations.label: Definition of ex(n, H) and equality ex(n, C_k) = f(0, 0, m_3(n), ..., m_{k-1}(n), 0, m_{k+1}(n), ..., m_n(n))
